Subject: Follow-up: PriimeHealth data handling & marketplace telemetry alignment

Hi Elena / Daniel — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps: 

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: PriimeHealth will call Redwood-hosted models from a marketplace listing to generate patient-facing summaries. Some inputs will include PII (patient name, DOB, limited PHI).
- Key risk areas you called out: PII handling, retention windows for telemetry/logs, auditability of calls, and third-party telemetry sharing via marketplace partners.

Open questions / action items (owner):
1) Retention policy for request/response payloads and aggregated telemetry (Logan) — provide default settings and options for extended retention.
2) Subprocessor roster & DPAs (Marissa) — deliver current list and any marketplace partner exceptions.
3) Example audit log extract and redaction options (Logan) — share redacted sample CSV.
4) KMS / customer-managed keys / encryption at rest (Stephanie) — confirm support and any constraints for Private/Dedicated.
5) SOC2 / compliance artifacts (Logan) — share latest report and SOC scope.

Attached: Priime_Questionnaire_v1.pdf (you filled during the call) — I’ve pulled the notes into our questionnaire.

Proposed cadence: Marissa and Stephanie to join a technical deep-dive with Priime security team next week to go over subprocessor details and retention tradeoffs. Are you available Wed 2028-07-20 or Thu 2028-07-21 in the morning PT?

Thanks — I’ll prepare the subprocessor list and the redacted log sample ahead of that meeting.

Best,

Logan — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: for audit purposes we require a 90-day default for request/response logs and 365 days for security/audit logs; anything less will need business justification. Can Redwood support tiered retention by environment (prod vs. staging) or by customer config?
- PII handling: we need to know whether Redwood stores full request/response payloads or an indexed hash only, and whether content redaction is available prior to storage.
- Marketplace flows: our marketplace requires that any telemetry shared with the marketplace operator be limited to metadata (latency, error counts) and not include message content; does Redwood have controls to block content-level telemetry to marketplace partners?

I’m attaching our internal security questionnaire (Priime_Security_Questionnaire_filled.docx). Please have Marissa review, and loop in your compliance team if needed.

We can do Wed 2028-07-20 10am PT for the deep-dive — Daniel and our security lead will be on the call.

Thanks,

Head of Product, PriimeHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: PriimeHealth data handling & marketplace telemetry alignment

Hi all — quick answers to the questionnaire items that matter for your risk review. Happy to cover more detail on the 7/20 deep-dive.

1) Retention windows:
- Default telemetry (metrics, aggregated error/latency): 30 days.
- Request/response logs: default 30 days for Hosted; configurable 90/365/indefinite on Dedicated and Private with admin controls. We can set retention per-customer on Dedicated and Private deployments via the Console.

2) PII storage & redaction:
- Hosted API: by default, we retain request/response payloads to support debugging and quality investigations. We also provide on-request redaction tooling (pre-ingest) and a setting to store only indexed hashes instead of full payloads for sensitive use cases.
- For Private and Dedicated customers we support an opt-in no-storage mode where payloads are not persisted beyond ephemeral runtime (except for traces/metrics), subject to feature parity and SLA implications.

3) Marketplace telemetry and third-party sharing:
- Redwood’s marketplace integration sends limited operational telemetry to marketplace operators (latency, success/failure counts, billing IDs). We do not send message content by default.
- We can enforce a configuration to route marketplace-related telemetry through a filtered pipeline that strips content-level fields prior to export.
- Any marketplace vendor that receives telemetry must be on our subprocessor roster and bound by contract (DPA + narrow usage restrictions).

4) KMS / encryption:
- We support customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS) for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers may use Redwood-managed keys by default; we can discuss HSM options for enterprise contracts.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
- Share current subprocessor roster and copy of typical DPA (Redwood_Subprocessors_2028-07.pdf).
- Provide a redacted sample audit log (sample_audit_log.csv) and our SOC2 Type II report (SOC2_Type2_2027.pdf).

If you have a specific retention policy requirement for PHI, flag it now so we can validate with engineering and legal.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Trust | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Elena / Daniel — attaching the materials Marissa referenced. Couple of concrete points and proposed agenda for the deep-dive on 2028-07-20 10am PT (confirmed earlier):

Attachments included:
- Redwood_Subprocessors_2028-07.pdf (current subprocessor roster and high-level vendor roles)
- SOC2_Type2_2027.pdf (selected excerpts relevant to data handling controls)
- sample_audit_log.csv (redacted, shows timestamp, request_id, anonymized user_id, latency_ms, error_code)

Concrete notes: 
- For Hosted: default payload retention is 30 days; we can configure redaction and hashed-only storage for sensitive fields but cannot guarantee 365-day retention without moving to Dedicated/Private.
- Marketplace exports: we will enable a filtered telemetry export pipeline for your listing that strips any content fields; marketplace operator will receive only metadata (latency, success/failure, billing tag).
- KMS: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS keys today; Hosted can be evaluated as part of an enterprise contract.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (30–45m):
1) Walk subprocessor roster and highlight marketplace partners. (Marissa)
2) Show Console retention controls and redaction UI. (Stephanie)
3) Review sample_audit_log and discuss retention SLA options. (Logan)
4) Next steps: DPA redlines and procurement timeline.

Next steps for Priime: confirm preferred retention for production (30 / 90 / 365 / no-storage) and any non-negotiable marketplace telemetry constraints.

Thanks — I’ll send calendar invite with the attachments.

Best,
Logan
